static_traits.name: Li Ming
static_traits.social_status: Weak social support system, tense relationships with friends due to blaming habits
static_traits.medical_history: No significant physical illness; has not yet received psychotherapy
static_traits.language_features: Fairly clear expression, somewhat negative attitude but willing to try small goals; when topics of responsibility and accountability are involved, easily avoids and blames others

basic_info.main_problem: I always blame my own faults on others, which makes me feel helpless and stuck in life.
basic_info.core_demands: I decided to seek counseling because I realize my pattern of blaming responsibility on others is hindering my Personal growth and mental-physical health.
growth_experiences: Long blamed by parents in adolescence, attributing all faults to oneself, thereby forming strong self-blame and helplessness; this pattern continued into adulthood, significantly worsening in the past two years due to Unemployment, unhealthy lifestyle and insufficient motivation, comprehensively affecting Interpersonal relationships, Work and health.

core_beliefs: I cannot control and improve my own life

special_situations.event: Looking in the mirror or down seeing one's obvious beer belly, realizing not seeing one's feet for two years
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If my physical condition is very poor and appearance bad, it shows I cannot change, the future will not improve either
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Giving up action, maintaining an unhealthy lifestyle, avoiding facing health topics

special_situations.event: Situations arise at work or in life that require taking responsibility and being held accountable (such as task failure or things going wrong)
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I admit my fault and take responsibility, I will be blamed by others and feel intense shame and guilt
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Shirks responsibility, blames others, avoids taking responsibility and explaining one's own faults
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: This is not my fault, it is others' problem

special_situations.event: Long-term job-search obstacles after Unemployment or thinking about being continuously Unemployed
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: One or several failures mean I will fail in all respects
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Reduces job-seeking actions, lowers investment, and attributes failure to the external environment
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I fail in every aspect, I cannot possibly improve the current situation

special_situations.event: When interacting with friends, having conflicts, or being questioned
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If admitting my own fault would lose face and the relationship, I can only protect myself by blaming the other party
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Immediately looking for others' mistakes, Reinforcing external attribution to maintain self-esteem
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: It is all their fault, they keep me stuck

core_conflict.wish: Longs to be treated fairly, free from blame, and to preserve self-esteem and a sense of worth
core_conflict.fear: Fearing taking responsibility will trigger shame, being blamed and controlled, ultimately being negated and abandoned
defense_goal: Alleviating guilt and shame by shirking responsibility and avoiding bearing it, maintaining fragile self-esteem and a sense of safety

object_relations.object_representation: Others who blame, criticize, and attribute all mistakes to oneself (internalized parental images)

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor invites him to take responsibility for own behavior or jointly discuss improvement plans
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Experiences this as possibly being blamed or blaming themselves like the parents (transference: experiencing the counselor as a harsh other)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Using an Empathic and non-judgmental tone, first validating their shame and helplessness, then inviting them to choose executable small steps in collaborative language, avoiding blame or coercion.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor suggests starting from small, realistic goals (such as a short walk every day)
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Believing small changes are meaningless, oneself cannot possibly improve (hopelessness)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Inviting them to try with an experimental mindset, using the language of 'let's test it together', providing observable indicators, reducing argument, and emphasizing self-choice and revocability.

manifestations: Long feeling trapped and helpless, believing change is meaningless
Holding a 'never possible' Anticipation toward health improvement
When needing to take responsibility, avoids it and shifts responsibility to others
Difficulty facing the Anxiety brought by choices and responsibilities

contact_model.definition: The individual attributes feelings they find hard to accept to others, corresponding to 'possession'.
manifestations: When discussing problems, emphasizes others as the main cause
When things go wrong, the first reaction is to look for others' faults

positive_force: Has a certain level of self-awareness, recognizing that the pattern of blaming others is hindering Personal growth and health
Willing to try small, feasible goals (such as a short daily walk)
No significant physical illness, with the basic conditions for engaging in healthy behaviors
negative_force: Long-term habits of thinking and behavior of blaming others and avoiding responsibility
Helplessness and anticipation of failure (catastrophizing, overgeneralization)
Insufficient motivation, difficulty persisting with change
Unhealthy lifestyle and lack of self-care
Weak social support system,Tense relationships with friends

target_behavior.behavior: When things go wrong, shirking responsibility and blaming others for faults
antecedent: Problems or failures at work or in life
Being asked by others to take responsibility or be held accountable
target_behavior.core_reason: Long-term parental blame in childhood formed high sensitivity to shame and guilt, avoiding self-blame and being blamed by blaming others
target_behavior.function: Avoiding unwelcome emotions (Guilt, shame) and external blame, temporarily maintaining self-esteem and a sense of control
target_behavior.consequence: Interpersonal tension, problems unable to be effectively resolved, stagnation and increased helplessness

target_behavior.behavior: Holding the belief that health improvement is 'never possible', leading to avoidance of exercise and self-care
antecedent: Seeing one's obvious beer belly or realizing one has not seen one's own feet for two years
Realizing one's health is not good and change is needed
target_behavior.core_reason: Catastrophizing and predicting the future lead one to negate the possibility of change, thus giving up action
target_behavior.function: Avoiding the risk of effort and failure, reducing present Anxiety and Sense of frustration
target_behavior.consequence: Health further declines, weight increases, Low mood and helplessness worsen

target_behavior.behavior: Lacking motivation to seek jobs and complete tasks, long-term Unemployment
target_behavior.core_reason: Overgeneralization and hopelessness make one believe effort will not bring change
target_behavior.function: Avoids possible rejection and failure, maintaining short-term emotional comfort
target_behavior.consequence: Continued Unemployment, financial and self-efficacy damage, helplessness and Increased stress
